# Card Visual Language v1

Machine-readable authority: `card_visual_language.json`. No final asset or runtime implementation is created by this specification.

## Schema Version

1

## Scope

Layout/state grammar for all 150 existing cards. No new card definitions, illustrations, costs, effects, levels or rarity classes.

## Rarities

Normal; Epic; Legendary

## Branches


| Field | Contract / value |
| --- | --- |
| single | one icon/name group below title |
| dual | two equal-sized icon/name groups on the same row, source order retained |
| overflow | compact label in market, full canonical branch names in inspection; no merged third branch symbol |

## States


| Field | Contract / value |
| --- | --- |
| selected | visual: focus border and explicit selection check/text; action: selection alone does not purchase |
| purchasable | visual: visible cost and enabled state; action: explicit buy/confirm affordance in inspection |
| unavailable | visual: muted rarity accent, lock/reason label; retain readable content; action: inspection stays available, purchase disabled |
| owned | visual: owned badge and current level; action: upgrade availability comes from canonical model, not artwork |
| maxed | visual: MAX badge and final level, no implied upgrade arrow; action: purchase/upgrade disabled when actual rules require |
| normal | visual: single neutral frame; action: neutral presentation |


## State Precedence

Maxed/unavailable governs purchase availability; selected is an independent overlay; owned and level persist. Rarity/branch identity never disappear under disabled styling.

## Level Policy

Display authoritative current/max level. The known Normal/Epic/Legendary level counts come from data; the proof uses explicitly synthetic display fixtures only.

## Text Overflow

Never shrink critical text below body minimum. Prefer two-line title, concise authored summary and full text in inspection. A future fourth/fifth card layout must be revalidated, not scaled down from this proof.

## Forbidden

Rare/Mythic labels from legacy frame sheet; hardcoded prices from reference images; level stars that contradict canonical data; color-only rarity/state; production use of unknown-rights illustrations
